subject: Strategy debrief — Q1 scoring, narrative, and quick wins
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strategy debrief — Q1 scoring, narrative, and quick wins

Team — attaching the consolidated Q1 scoring workbook (Q1_scores_v3.xlsx) and the raw retrospective notes. I pulled together the baseline numbers and a first-pass narrative (draft_exec_narrative_v1.docx).

Top-level asks:
- Quick read-through of the scoring sheet and flag any obvious data issues (laura/marcus) by 1pm PT.
- Recommend one framing paragraph for the exec narrative (vivek) — focus: growth vs reliability trade-offs.
- Two tactical quick wins that can move a metric by E2E (tessa/lauren).

Notes/highlights:
- We hit 88% of the customer latency target (vs 95% goal) due to the billing connector migration in Feb — flagged in the sheet as "platform headwind".
- Revenue expansion is 7% QoQ; below plan because of delayed pilot closes at Acme Corp (see HubSpot HS-4521).
- Team engagement and hiring OTE improved; hiring lag remains on infra roles.

I want a short summary paragraph we can drop into the QBR deck and an annotated list of corrections to the scores. I'll compile & send to execs by 5pm PT.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Head of Growth Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q1_scores_v3.xlsx, team_retrospective_notes.pdf, draft_exec_narrative_v1.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategy debrief — Q1 scoring, narrative, and quick wins

Jonas — I skimmed the scoring workbook. A few quick items: 
- Row 12 (Product growth) should use the final telemetry export (sheet 'metrics_final'), current value looks like draft export from 3/18. I flagged it and added the corrected number in column AH.
- We should separate 'platform headwind' into two tags: migration-related vs infra-capacity. That will help the narrative be more precise.
- Suggest we move the hiring OTE improvement to a separate HR slide rather than burying it in the scorecard.

I'm OK with the revenue framing but think we should call out Acme's pilot delay explicitly (they pushed to June). Marcus — can you confirm the ARR impact?

Quick note: I added two comments in the docx about tone (soft on missed targets, firm on mitigation).

- Laura
Laura Bennett | VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategy debrief — Q1 scoring, narrative, and quick wins

Agree with Laura. Two tactical quick wins from my side that we can list: 
1) Enable unblock for the billing connector rollback path (2 engineers, 3 days) — estimated 1.5% latency recovery within a week.
2) Short-term inference cache warmth for top 50 enterprise routes (config + deploy) — ~1.2% cost savings and smoother p95.

I can own #1; Lauren can take #2 with Marcus helping on infra rollout.

—Tessa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategy debrief — Q1 scoring, narrative, and quick wins

Team — thanks for the quick turn. A few framing suggestions for the executive narrative: 
- Lead with customer impact: "Mitigations ahead; pilots delayed at two logos, which drove near-term expansion misses; platform migration introduced transient latency pressure."
- Signal ownership and timelines (e.g., "Rollback path ready by 4/9; pilot rebaseline by 6/1").
- For the Board, emphasize the longer-term levers (routing policy, caching, Dedicated adoption) rather than tactical fixes.

I'll draft a 3-paragraph version and drop in the Drive link by 3pm. We should aim to keep the QBR slide to a single 'scorecard + 3 bullets' frame.

Vivek

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com

Great input — thank you. Finalizing next steps and owners below; I'll send the compiled narrative to execs and the Board by 5pm PT.

- Data corrections & final score refresh (Laura, Marcus) — due 1:00pm PT.
- Rollback path and latency quick-win (Tessa) — plan by 4/7, implementation 4/9–4/12.
- Cache warmth pilot plan (Lauren, Marcus) — plan by 4/9.
- Exec narrative 3-paragraph draft (Vivek) — deliver by 3:00pm PT (please drop in Drive).
- Final QBR slide & send to Board (Jonas) — 5:00pm PT.

I've updated the Drive folder with the latest files: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQ1scores (see draft_exec_narrative_v1.docx -> draft_exec_narrative_v2.docx).

If anyone has redlines after I share with execs, ping me directly. I'll also include a one-paragraph 'what we learned' for the ops and product teams.

-Jonas
